scope: WebAssembly release only. Three paired fresh Node processes per workload, alternating baseline/candidate, pinned to CPU 2, SLOPPY_THREADS=1. Program timers exclude startup; runtime tiering work during kernels is included. Other user work was not stopped. Build times are single observations. Native inlining policy is unchanged.
change: On the wasm target, leave functions containing loops as calls instead of expanding their bodies during release inlining.

mechanism_evidence.ir: Baseline release main contains the particle update loop and no separate step function; candidate retains f_step and calls it.

interpretation: The particle slowdown is consistent with lost tier-up opportunities after loop inlining: default V8 execution improves 2.46x, while forcing optimized compilation makes baseline/candidate comparable. Baseline-only V8 execution is modestly slower with the retained call. Helpers and records improve about 2x and 2.5x; other workloads are smaller changes. Seven additional paired text runs have medians 116.02/116.70ms (0.6% difference). Results are Node/V8 evidence, not cross-browser performance guarantees.
harness_source:
# Platform boundary for the Dewy application benchmarks. The original
# harness uses compiler-specific raw syscalls; this uses the core's library.
size_argument = (values: str[], fallback: int) -> int:
    if values.len() < 2: return fallback
    text = values[1]
    value = 0
    loop byte in text:
        if byte < 48 or byte > 57: return fallback
        value = value * 10 + int(byte) - 48
        if value > 1000000000: return fallback
    value

clock = () -> int: time_ns()
mix = (hash: int, value: int) -> int: __floor_mod(hash * 31 + value, 1000000007)
